v.why: Adding the 0->3 identity shortcut where none exists restores the residual path and gives much larger gains than replacing an existing conv or pool there.
Deleting the input-to-output skip removes the cell's residual connection, which hurts far more than deleting a conv on that edge.
With edge 1->3 already absent, removing edge 0->3 leaves very few paths into the output node, which badly degrades trainability.
When node 1 is disconnected from the input, edge 0->3 is one of the only remaining routes to the output, so removing it is especially damaging.
When there is no 0->3 shortcut, a skip on 2->3 supplies an alternative short gradient path, so the edit helps more.
Replacing a parameter-free pooling op on the first edge with a 3x3 conv adds useful capacity, a larger gain than swapping out skip, 1x1 conv, or none.
Removing a harmful avg_pool on edge 0 costs little or helps, whereas removing a conv or skip there loses useful signal.
Swapping a pooling op on edge 1->3 for a 3x3 conv converts a weak edge into a strong one, giving larger gains than replacing none, skip, or 1x1 conv.
Replacing avg_pool on edge 0->2 with a 3x3 conv adds learnable features where pooling contributed little, so it beats replacing skip or none.
Turning a skip on the final edge into pooling costs little, while turning a conv into pooling removes important capacity right before the output.
